description: The people your own People Searches found, as CSV or JSON Lines text: one search (task_id), or everyone found on one platform (platform, with the same q, sort, and filters as people-profiles). Free: it reads people your earlier searches found and runs no new search. The reply is a note with the row count, then the file text cut at a row boundary to max_rows rows and 50,000 characters; the note says how many rows were cut and where to get the whole file. CSV keeps its header row. The data came from public profiles and posts, with only the contacts each person lists publicly.

has.description: Channels every person must have, example: ['email']. 'email' is a public email; the others are a link of that type.

location.description: Text in the location, example: 'united states'.

max_rows.description: Most rows to return (1-1000, default 100). The reply also stops before 50,000 characters of file text.

platform.description: Without task_id: export everyone found on 'x', 'youtube', 'linkedin', or 'tiktok'.

q.description: Platform export only: text in the name, handle, bio, or location.

task_id.description: Export one search: the task_id returned by people-search. Omit it and set platform to export everyone your searches found on that platform.

verified.description: Only verified accounts. Only X and TikTok people carry a verified flag.

name: people-search-export
title: Export People Found
